definitions.explanation: A door or opening designated for escaping a building during a fire, earthquake, or other emergency. Standard wording on safety signage and in fire-code documents.

examples.japanese: {避難口|ひなんぐち}を{確認|かくにん}してください。
examples.english: Please check where the emergency exits are.

examples.japanese: {避難口|ひなんぐち}の{前|まえ}に{物|もの}を{置|お}かないでください。
examples.english: Please do not place objects in front of the emergency exit.

examples.japanese: {煙|けむり}が{充満|じゅうまん}する{前|まえ}に、{一番|いちばん}{近|ちか}い{避難口|ひなんぐち}から{外|そと}へ{出|で}た。
examples.english: Before the smoke filled the room, we got outside through the nearest emergency exit.

notes:
Formed from {避難|ひなん} (evacuation, taking refuge) plus 〜{口|ぐち} (opening, gateway), which voices to ぐち in compounds.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {避難口|ひなんぐち}{誘導灯|ゆうどうとう}: emergency exit guidance light
- {避難口|ひなんぐち}を{塞|ふさ}ぐ: to block an emergency exit
- {最寄|もよ}りの{避難口|ひなんぐち}: the nearest emergency exit

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {非常口|ひじょうぐち}: emergency exit — far more common in everyday speech and on green exit signs; {避難口|ひなんぐち} is the more technical, fire-code term
